does: Collapses tender leaves with brief heat, so that they turn soft and dark and lose most of their bulk.
how: Wash the leaves and leave the water that clings to them.
Melt a little fat in a wide pan over medium heat.
Add the leaves by the handful, turning them as they fall.
Take them off the heat as soon as the last leaf has collapsed, and press out the water.

cues.text: Dark green, glossy and limp, a fraction of the raw heap.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the leaves on the heat, so that they go on shedding water and turn slimy.
mistakes.fix: Stop the moment they collapse, and drain them.
